Applied from the review: Huesca gain 1096-11 plus siege war; Huesca cell and the seven Graus-Barbastro cells cut from the 1043-1082 shapes and the 1043 and 1076 gains; 1099 and 1100 notes rewritten; Tudela counterpart almoravid-dynasty (and dated 25 February 1119 from es.wikipedia); Peter I to 1104 (Peter I page); thin items Barbastro 1064-1065 (contest and war) and Tauste 1146 (contest and war, García Ramírez page) added; Urraca page and es Ramiro I page tried and left as bridges.

The reviewer's 'check that the 1099 and 1111 shapes agree' found 12 of Cliopatria's 19 new 1111 cells unexplained; the Alfonso I page dates Ejea and Tauste to 1105 and Tamarite de Litera and San Esteban de Litera to 1107, so two gains and five stepped keyframes (1083, 1089, 1100, 1105, 1107) were added. Every gain region from 1043 to 1146 was checked by grid to lie in the shape of its year and not in the shape of the year before.

Page conflict: the Peter I page puts the Battle of Alcoraz in 1095 and the fall of Huesca on 27 November 1095; the Battle of Alcoraz page (15 November 1096), the Kingdom page and taifa-of-zaragoza (1096-11) agree on 1096, which the dossier uses.

Cross-dossier items for the eu-12 owners: taifa-of-zaragoza lacks 1105 and 1107 losses and the Barbastro and Tauste contests; taifa-of-lerida should move Monzón to 1089 and add the 1064-1065 Barbastro contest; almoravid-dynasty needs the 1119 Tudela loss; kingdom-of-castile needs the 1126 loss and 1127 gain.

Seven pages opened in the repair (Battle of Alcoraz, Peter I, Siege of Barbastro, Urraca, es Ramiro I, es Tudela, García Ramírez) plus Kingdom of Navarre (silent on Tauste, not cited) and a reopened Alfonso I: over the original budget of five, at the reviewer's request.
